messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY: High error rate for customer AquilaSys (Private VPC). Observed: 502/503 responses from model endpoints behind tenant NLB. Impact: degraded inference for dedicated pool. Paging oncall.

sara: I'm on it, taking primary. Can someone confirm if this is only egress or ingress too? :eyes:

matt: I see healthcheck failures from the NLB to the node pool around 02:18 UTC. Connection resets, TLS handshake timeouts.

diego: Oncall network — running quick check on SG rules and NLB target health. Giving me 1-2 mins.

jess: Reached out to AquilaSys ops contact aisha to let them know we're investigating. aisha, FYI you might see intermittent 503s.

aisha-customer: Thanks, Jess. Confirming customer telemetry shows spikes aligned with your alert. Latency spikes also, a few customer requests timed out.

eng-network: Quick findings: two nodes in the dedicated pool marked unhealthy by NLB. Health check path /_health returned 502 from upstream on those hosts. No recent SG changes in our audit logs.

sara: Ok, next steps — isolate whether node-level service is crashing or NLB healthcheck mismatch (TTL/caching/DNS). Diego, can you tail the container logs on the affected hosts? Matt, can you check NLB healthcheck config and LB connection reuse?

diego: Tailing logs: seeing repeated KV cache read errors and a short spike of OOM-kill in one container at 02:17:42. Stack snippet: ```
Sep 02 02:17:42 instance-12 kubelet: oom-kill: memory cgroup invoked kill process 42781 (redwood-server)
Sep 02 02:17:43 redwood-server[42781]: ERROR: failed to load kv cache: checksum mismatch
```

matt: NLB healthcheck config: TCP/443 to node IPs, interval 10s, unhealthy threshold 2. There was a flurry of TCP resets from the nodes starting 02:17:40. Suggesting host-level instability.

sara: That aligns with OOMs. But customer sees DNS TTL mismatch messages occasionally — could cached DNS entries be routing to drained hosts? Any stale records?

eng-network: Checked internal DNS (Consul) — services updated, TTL=30s. However, we saw /etc/resolv.conf on instance-12 pointed to a stale resolver during the spike (stale DHCP lease). ops-bot, any recent DHCP or VPC metadata changes?

ops-bot: No infra control-plane changes in the last 24h. Autoscaler has scaled recently for load spike at 02:10 UTC.

sara: Action plan: 1) cordon & drain instance-12 from pool, 2) restart affected container with memory limits adjusted, 3) force NLB re-registration after node recovers, 4) ask customer to clear local DNS cache if they persist. Doable?

diego: Cordon + drain in progress. Draining connections (conn-drain 300s). Starting memory-limited restart with env REDWOOD_MAX_CACHE=512MB.

matt: I'm forcing a re-register of healthy targets after drain completes. Will also temporarily relax NLB unhealthy threshold to 4 to avoid flapping during recovery.

aisha-customer: We'll flush our app-level DNS cache and retry. Appreciate the quick triage. Keeping customer informed.

eng-network: Drained instance-12. New pod started on instance-15, healthchecks green. NLB target health reports 4/4 healthy after re-register.

sara: Monitoring for 10m window. Can everyone post status updates in this thread. Matt, please note the config tweak so we can revert post-incident.

matt: Noted. Changed unhealthy threshold to 4 at 02:35 UTC. Will revert after 30m stable.

diego: Restarted container with memory cap. No more OOMs in logs. KV checksum errors not reappearing.

sara: Customer impact: 02:17–02:34 UTC partial service degradation for AquilaSys (~12% requests returned 502/503). Ticket #INC-2026-512 created and assigned to postmortem.

aisha-customer: Confirmed client traffic back to normal. We'll keep monitoring and reach out if we see recurrence. Thanks for the rapid response. :tada:

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: runbook 'vpc-private-egress-oom' executed: cordon/drain -> restart -> re-register -> monitor.

eng-network: Follow-ups: (1) add a guard in autoscaler to avoid simultaneous allocation leading to low memory situations, (2) increase healthcheck grace period for short OOM bursts, (3) verify DHCP lease renewal behavior on our AMI build.

sara: Agreed. I'll own the postmortem and remediation list. Assigning owners: Diego (container memory limits), Matt (NLB thresholds rollback + monitoring), Eng-network (DHCP/AMI investigation), Jess (customer comms).

matt: Rolling back unhealthy threshold to 2 at 03:05 UTC after 30m stable. All metrics look nominal.

sara: Closing incident thread — moving to postmortem doc. If anything reoccurs ping #eng-oncall. :lock:
